title: Joining Granny Squares
description: Connect finished granny squares into a larger piece with neat seams and even alignment.

content.summary: Learn how to line up corners, match stitch counts, and join squares without twisting or stretching them.
content.whyItMatters: Many beginner-friendly blankets, totes, and pillows are just smaller motifs joined well. The joining step is what makes them feel finished.
steps: Lay the squares flat with the right sides facing the same direction and match the corners first.
Choose a joining method such as whip stitch, slip stitch, or single crochet join depending on the look you want.
Join one seam at a time and check that the stitch counts stay aligned across both edges.
After joining, smooth the seam with your fingers and weave in the tails before adding the next section.
content.practice: Make two granny squares and join one full side using whip stitch, then compare it with a second sample joined using slip stitch.
commonMistakes: Joining mismatched corners and ending up with a twisted square layout.
Pulling the seam too tight so the joined edge buckles.
